outlooks.summary: Scattered to isolated severe storms are possible Saturday afternoon and evening from the Midwest west-southwestward to Kansas, as well as across the central and southern High Plains. Large hail and damaging wind will be the primary threats.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: A persistent large-scale pattern over the U.S. is progged to remain largely unchanged today, with cyclonic flow over both the north-central and eastern states, and the West, separated by a ridge that extends from Texas north-northwestward across the Rockies. At the surface, a weak cool front is forecast to shift southeastward across the Great Lakes/Midwest states and central Plains, as a short-wave disturbance aloft shifts southeastward in cyclonic/northwesterly flow aloft. This front will likely serve as a focus for scattered strong/severe storm development during the afternoon and evening hours. ...Southern Upper Great Lakes/Midwest west-southwestward to Kansas... As the cold front advances southeastward across the Great Lakes/upper Midwest/central Plains region during the day, this boundary should focus development of scattered showers and thunderstorm, as warm-sector heating/destabilization occurs. Aided by moderate northwesterly flow aloft, storms -- and associated risk for damaging winds and hail locally -- may move rather quickly southeastward, merging into clusters locally. The greatest coverage of severe storms appears to evolve from portions of central Illinois into centr

sections.title: Central and southern High Plains and vicinity
sections.text: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms are forecast to develop across portions of eastern Colorado this afternoon in a weak post-frontal upslope flow regime, with isolated storms also likely to evolve southward across the southern High Plains as a weak upper disturbance shifts northeastward through background anticyclonic flow aloft. The storms will be supported by diurnal heating over the High Plains resulting in ample destabilization, but the overall coverage/intensity of storms should be at least somewhat limited by the rather strong ridging aloft. Still, with moderate southwesterly flow at mid levels atop low-level southerly/southeasterly winds, shear will support organized multicell to weakly rotating storms. Large hail will likely be the primary risk initially, though locally damaging winds will be possible. During the evening, as a southerly low-level jet develops over the southern High Plains, this may support an upscale-growing cluster of storms, that may shift southeastward out of the High Plains, and toward central Kansas, central Oklahoma, and north Texas overnight. Potential for locally damaging winds may thus increase a bit during the evening, along with some risk for hail

outlooks.summary: Widely scattered severe thunderstorms are expected mainly this afternoon and evening from Lake Michigan vicinity southwestward to the central/southern High Plains. Large hail and damaging winds will be the primary threats.

sections.title: Missouri/Illinois/Indiana to Wisconsin/Lower Michigan
sections.text: An upper trough will continue to gradually amplify over northern Ontario today, with a strengthening belt of cyclonically curved westerlies aloft overspreading the Great Lakes region. On the southern fringe of this more pronounced trough, a lower amplitude mid-level trough over southern Minnesota/northern Iowa at mid-morning will continue generally eastward through the afternoon/early evening. Weak surface cyclogenesis is expected along a front in the general vicinity of southern Lake Michigan toward southern Ontario through evening, with a cold front otherwise advancing southeastward across the Midwest through tonight. There still remains some short-term uncertainty regarding the most probable corridors of where severe thunderstorms will occur later today, although at least widely scattered to scattered severe thunderstorms are expected over a broad portion of the Midwest to Great Lakes. Initial thunderstorm intensification/severe threat will probably develop across southern Wisconsin/northern Illinois into Lower Michigan this afternoon, with other storms increasing with southwestward extent across Illinois/Missouri along the advancing cold front, as it intercepts a very unstable

sections.title: Central/southern High Plains
sections.text: An upper-level ridge will remain centered over the region with weak to slight height rises generally expected, although mid-level temperatures will not be overly warm by late spring standards. Initially, aided by a modest low-level jet/elevated moisture transport, a couple of strong to locally severe storms could occur early today across southwest Kansas and possibly into northwest Oklahoma, although effective shear will generally weaken with southeastward extent. Otherwise, aided by low-level upslope flow/orographic lift, widely scattered thunderstorms are initially expected to develop this afternoon across a broad north-to-south expanse of the High Plains from southeast Wyoming/eastern Colorado into eastern New Mexico and far west Texas, with richer low-level moisture found across the southern High Plains. Additional, at least isolated, surface-based development appears likely by late afternoon/early evening within a very unstable air mass along the southward-sagging front as it extends east-northeastward along the Kansas/Oklahoma border vicinity. outlooks.summary: Widely scattered severe thunderstorms are expected mainly this afternoon and evening from Lake Michigan vicinity southwestward to the central/southern High Plains. Large hail and damaging winds will be the primary threats. Water vapor imagery shows a well-defined shortwave trough over IA. This feature will track east-southeastward into parts of IL/IN this afternoon and evening, providing large-scale ascent and aiding in the development of scattered thunderstorms. Multiple clusters of storms are expected today, with each holding some risk of severe weather.

sections.title: MI/OH
sections.text: Thunderstorms currently over southwest Lower MI are expected to track eastward and intensify later today as they approach western Lake Erie. These storms will then continue eastward across southeast Lower MI and northern OH, with the potential for damaging winds and hail. Refer to MCD #919 for further details.

sections.title: WI/IL
sections.text: Other strong storms are expected to form this afternoon near the surface low over southern WI and northern IL. Forecast soundings in this area suggest large CAPE values and sufficient vertical shear for a few organized multicell or occasional supercell structures, capable of large hail and damaging winds.

sections.title: IL/MO
sections.text: By mid afternoon, thunderstorms are expected to form along a cold front sagging across northwest IL and northern MO. These storms will be near the core of stronger midlevel winds associated with the shortwave trough, and in region where model guidance provides highest confidence of longer-lived storms and possible supercells. This activity should spread southeastward across the ENH risk area through the evening with a threat of damaging wind gusts and large hail. Very large hail is possible with initial supercells.

sections.title: NM/TX/OK
sections.text: A midlevel ridge axis extends from southeast CO into west TX. However, several subtle impulses are noted in water vapor imagery over this area, and 12z model guidance shows neutral to slightly falling midlevel heights later today. This will likely lead to scattered thunderstorms throughout the southern high Plains. Forecast soundings suggest sufficient vertical shear for a few supercells - capable of hail and damaging wind gusts. This activity will likely persist much of the night and spread into OK, although the severe risk is expected to slowly diminish. ..Hart/Wendt.. 06/01/2019

outlooks.summary: Widely scattered severe thunderstorms are expected mainly the rest of this afternoon and evening from Lake Michigan vicinity southwestward to the central/southern High Plains. Large hail and damaging winds will be the primary threats.

sections.title: 20Z Update
sections.text: The primary change with the 20Z outlook is to lower severe probabilities in the wake of the ongoing MCSs across southeast MI and also across OK. There is some potential for redevelopment of thunderstorms across both of those regions later tonight, but the prospect for recovery seems too limited to support more than marginal severe probabilities for the remainder of the period. Otherwise, scattered severe thunderstorms remain possible across portions of the central/southern High Plains, Midwest, and lower Great Lakes. There is some uncertainty regarding the coverage of thunderstorms within the Enhanced Risk area across MO/IL, though this region still appears conditionally favorable for severe hail/wind with any sustained convection very late this afternoon into the evening. ..Dean.. 06/01/2019 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1104 AM CDT Sat Jun 01 2019/ Water vapor imagery shows a well-defined shortwave trough over IA. This feature will track east-southeastward into parts of IL/IN this afternoon and evening, providing large-scale ascent and aiding in the development of scattered thunderstorms. Multiple clusters of storms are expected today, with each holding some risk of severe weather.

sections.title: MI/OH
sections.text: Thunderstorms currently over southwest Lower MI are expected to track eastward and intensify later today as they approach western Lake Erie. These storms will then continue eastward across southeast Lower MI and northern OH, with the potential for damaging winds and hail. Refer to MCD #919 for further details.

sections.title: WI/IL
sections.text: Other strong storms are expected to form this afternoon near the surface low over southern WI and northern IL. Forecast soundings in this area suggest large CAPE values and sufficient vertical shear for a few organized multicell or occasional supercell structures, capable of large hail and damaging winds.

sections.title: IL/MO
sections.text: By mid afternoon, thunderstorms are expected to form along a cold front sagging across northwest IL and northern MO. These storms will be near the core of stronger midlevel winds associated with the shortwave trough, and in region where model guidance provides highest confidence of longer-lived storms and possible supercells. This activity should spread southeastward across the ENH risk area through the evening with a threat of damaging wind gusts and large hail. Very large hail is possible with initial supercells.

sections.title: NM/TX/OK
sections.text: A midlevel ridge axis extends from southeast CO into west TX. However, several subtle impulses are noted in water vapor imagery over this area, and 12z model guidance shows neutral to slightly falling midlevel heights later today. This will likely lead to scattered thunderstorms throughout the southern high Plains. Forecast soundings suggest sufficient vertical shear for a few supercells - capable of hail and damaging wind gusts. This activity will likely persist much of the night and spread into OK, although the severe risk is expected to slowly diminish.

outlooks.summary: Scattered severe thunderstorms will continue this evening from the southern High Plains, across the lower Missouri Valley, into portions of Ohio. Large hail and damaging winds remain the primary threats.

sections.title: 01z Update
sections.text: Considerable amount of strong convection has developed along a corridor from eastern NM-TX Panhandle-MO/IL-northwest OH. Severe probabilities have been adjusted in the wake of this activity to reflect overturned air mass where robust convection is not anticipated over the next few hours. Otherwise, severe probs have been increased across portions of north-central TX in response to scattered storms that continue to propagate south of the Red River region. Large hail and damaging winds remain possible with the strongest storms, especially with organized convection surging south across the St. Louis metro and over the southern High Plains. ..Darrow.. 06/02/2019

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Increased thunderstorm coverage is expected across southern Lower MI and adjacent portions of far northeast IN and far northwest OH. Trends will be monitored for possible watch issuance.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Air mass downstream of the area of thunderstorms moving across southern Lake Michigan continues to destabilize amidst partly cloudy skies. Recent observations reveal temperatures in the mid 70s and dewpoints in the mid 60s across southern Lower MI, south of an outflow boundary produced from early storms now moving into southwestern Ontario. Temperatures to the north of the boundary remain the 60s with dewpoints in the upper 50s/low 60s. Limited destabilization is expected north of the outflow but forecast soundings suggest that nearly all the convective inhibition within air mass south of the boundary has eroded and recent mesoanalysis estimates MLCAPE around 1500 J/kg. The stronger mid-level flow and better vertical shear will be displaced north of the better instability (i.e. across northern Lower MI) but a few stronger storms capable of hail and damaging wind gusts are possible. Overall thunderstorms coverage is uncertain, but convective trends will be monitored closely and a watch may eventually be needed if trends suggest sufficient storm coverage and intensity.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Trends will be monitored closely for potential re-intensification of the ongoing convective cluster moving across western OK.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Area of thunderstorms currently over northwest OK continues to push southeastward at around 25 kt. A weakening trend has been noted over the past hour or so, with echo tops decreasing and weaker low-level reflectivity noted along the leading edge. The cool pool is visible on satellite imagery over the northeast TX Panhandle to east-central TX Panhandle/OK border but has yet to outrun the convective cluster over most of OK. This gives some uncertainty as to whether or not the weakening trend will actually continue. Mesoanalysis suggests the downstream air mass across western OK/eastern TX Panhandle is uncapped and estimates MLCAPE over 2000 J/kg. An instability gradient exists farther east across central OK where lower dewpoints and slightly cooler temperatures result in a weakly capped and less unstable environment. Thermodynamic trends within the downstream environment suggest an eventual re-intensification of the line is possible, likely over western OK and adjacent portions of the eastern TX Panhandle. However, large-scale forcing for ascent is negligible with heights across the region likely rising slightly. These competing factors result in uncertainty regarding the short-term convective evolution. This uncertainty leads to low watch probability, but trends will be monitored closely.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A few damaging wind gusts will be possible with storms that develop/move into the discussion area. Marginally severe hail may also occur with any stronger storms. A WW is not expected, but convective trends will be monitored.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A few storms have initiated along/near a weak surface boundary in far southwestern New York in the last 30 minutes. Furthermore, activity now moving across central Lake Erie is expected to impact far western New York and northwest Pennsylvania in the next hour or so. Surface temperatures have risen to the low to mid 70s F with dewpoints in the upper 50s F to lower 60s F allowing for modest buoyancy of 500-1000 J/kg MLCAPE. Though low-level flow is weak, per regional VAD profiles, fairly steep low-level lapse rates will allow a few water-loaded downdrafts to generate a damaging wind gusts. Mid-level lapse rates near 8 C/km will also support a marginal severe hail threat, though modest deep-layer shear and storm mode will limit this threat. A WW is not currently anticipated given the marginal nature of the threat, though trends will continue to be monitored for increases in intensity/coverage.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Increasing thunderstorm coverage is expected from far northeast NM southwestward across the TX Panhandle. Damaging wind gusts and hail are possible with the stronger storms.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Visible satellite imagery shows most of the low clouds present this morning over the TX Panhandle and vicinity have eroded, with deepening cumulus clouds now in place. Recent surface analysis places a outflow boundary from near the western border of the TX/OK Panhandles southwestward into western OK. Some surface troughing is also noted a bit farther west/northwest into northwest NM. Attempts at deep convection have been noted over the past hour with convective initiation now realized across the east-central TX Panhandle and over far northeast NM. Continued heating and resulting destabilization is anticipated near these boundaries with a gradual increase in thunderstorm coverage anticipated. Forecast soundings and mesoanalysis suggest vertical shear is modest but still sufficient for occasionally organized storms. Deeply mixed boundary layer and dry mid-levels suggest the primary threat is strong wind gusts, although some hail is also possible.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated hail and/or damaging wind gusts possible over the next few hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Recent mesoanalysis indicates the air mass downstream of the outflow boundary surging southward across western OK is characterized by 2000+ J/kg of MLCAPE and no convective inhibition. Cool air behind this outflow boundary will likely limit storm longevity but interaction with the boundary could briefing augment updrafts with any ongoing activity. Visible satellite imagery shows increasing deep convection just southwest of SPS. Anticipated interaction between these storms and the ongoing outflow boundary may result in stronger updrafts than would typically be expected within the weakly sheared environment. Isolated hail and/or damaging wind gusts are the primary threat. There is some potential for the development of a more linear system along this outflow, with a result threat downstream for damaging wind gusts. However, given the lack of stronger large-scale forcing for ascent and dependence on mesoscale factors, the overall convective evolution is uncertain.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorms have initiated in southwest Wisconsin with an increase in coverage expected into more of southern Wisconsin and northern Illinois. Damaging wind gusts and severe hail will be the primary threats. A WW will likely be needed soon.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Thunderstorms have developed near the Dane/Iowa County, WI border in the last hour. Activity has been weak thus far given the ample amounts of cloud cover across much of southern Wisconsin. Southeastern Wisconsin and northern Illinois have remained relatively cloud free and have warmed to mid 70s F to low 80s F, away from the influence of the lake breeze. Objective mesoanalysis shows MLCAPE reaching 1000-1500 J/kg south of the warm frontal boundary. Moderate mid-level flow of around 40 kts will foster enough deep-layer shear for storm organization into multicells with perhaps a few supercell structures as well. Greatest threat will likely be damaging wind gusts, particularly where greatest insolation/low-level lapse rates exists. Transient low-level rotation will also be possible near the boundary where winds are most backed. However, overall weak low-level flow and storm mode issues will greatly limit tornado potential. A WW is likely to be issued soon.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated damaging wind gusts are possible across the Ozark Plateau this afternoon. Marginal nature of severe threat will likely preclude the need for a watch.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Cumulus field over the Ozark Plateau has increased over the past hour with deeper convection and lightning now noted across Douglas and Texas Counties in south-central MO. RAP forecast soundings modified for current observations suggest MLCAPE around 1500 J/kg and well-mixed boundary layer extending up just past 850 mb. The environment is weakly sheared, suggestive of predominantly multicellular storms with only occasional updraft organization. Even so, the well-mixed boundary-layer coupled with relatively dry mid-levels will promote the potential for isolated damaging wind gusts. Marginal nature of the threat will likely preclude watch issuance.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Storms are currently moving out of WW 302 and it will likely be cancelled before 4 PM EDT. A small bowing segment will likely impact portions of northern Ohio in the next few hours. A WW probably will be needed to address the threat for damaging winds and severe hail.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Much of the ongoing linear MCS has moved out eastern lower Michigan and WW 302. Remaining counties will likely be cleared before the scheduled expiration of 4 PM EDT. As this activity moves over Lake Erie, there is uncertainty with regard to whether the MCS will be able to maintain its intensity farther downstream. Latest visible satellite imagery shows storms developing along the southern flank of the MCS in northwestern Ohio. While MLCAPE values have risen to 1000-1500 J/kg in northern Ohio, deep-layer shear remains quite weak. The greatest threat with storms along the Lake Erie coast in Ohio will likely be a few damaging wind gusts associated with a well developed cold pool. At its current pace of around 40 kts, the small bowing segment along the western Lake Erie shores will impact portions of northern Ohio in the next few hours. A watch will probably be needed to address this threat. ..Wendt.. 06/01/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorm coverage is expected to increase along and ahead of cold front moving into eastern KS, northern MO, and far southeastern IA. Hail and damaging wind gusts are possible and a watch will likely be needed across portions of the region.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Recent surface analysis places a cold front from southern WI southwestward across southeast IA, northwest MO, and eastern KS. A weak surface trough also exists ahead of this cold front from EMP (in east-central KS) northeastward to just north of MKC and then eastward across central MO. Thus far, deep convection along the front has struggled to persist, likely a result of modest convective inhibition. Some deeper convection has been noted across east-central IA along the front but the expectation is for convection to continue struggling along the front until it reaches farther southeast (i.e. northern MO and far southeast IA/west-central IL) where warmer temperatures and better low-level moisture exists. In these areas, little to no convective inhibition remains. Attempts at deeper convection along the surface trough are expected to eventually succeed, resulting in an overall increase in thunderstorm activity across the region. Air mass is characterized by enough instability and vertical shear to support storm/updraft organization. The primary severe threat appears to be damaging wind gusts, although the cool mid-level temperatures (i.e. -13 to -14 deg C at 500 mb) will likely support some hail as well. Convective trends will be monitored closely and watch will likely be needed across portions of the area.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The threat for isolated large hail and locally damaging wind gusts continues into the evening across WW #303.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Latest regional radar/lightning analysis continues to indicate periodic/brief updraft intensification associated with multicellular convection across WW #303. The environment over the area is characterized by MLCAPE between 1000-1500 J/kg and effective bulk shear of 20-30 knots (locally greater), which will support pulse-type severe thunderstorms. As such, isolated instances of large hail and locally damaging wind gusts will remain possible within the strongest thunderstorm cores into this evening. ..Elliott.. 06/01/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A few severe thunderstorms are possible along an outflow boundary into early evening. The need for watch issuance in the short term is uncertain at this time.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Strong thunderstorms have recently developed along an outflow boundary across northern Indiana. Sufficient heating/moisture has resulted in the development of MLCAPE into the 1500-2000 J/kg range to the warm side of the boundary. Effective shear of 25-35 kt will support some organized storm structures along and to the immediate cool side of the boundary. Steep lapse rates and cool temperatures aloft will support a hail threat with the strongest cells, while a localized damaging wind threat may also develop, especially with any upscale growth that occurs later in the convective evolution. Additional convection is developing upstream across southern WI and northern IL, which will move into the region toward evening. Watch issuance is possible if ongoing convection increases in coverage or if upstream convection become more organized as it approaches the area.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Large to very large hail is possible with the more intense supercells expected to develop this afternoon into the early evening.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Visible satellite/radar imagery shows rapid storm development from southeastern NM into Far West TX. Recent MRMS MESH data indicate hail potentially as large as 2.5-3.0 inches in diameter in southeast NM with a couple of supercells. Surface observations show moist/easterly component to the flow with upper 50s to lower 60s dewpoints. Steep lapse rates coupled with a relatively moist airmass are yielding a moderate to very unstable boundary layer (2000-3000 J/kg MLCAPE) amidst 50kt effective shear. As storms develop, expecting the stronger storms to intensify into supercells and be capable of large to very large hail (1-3 inches in diameter) and isolated severe gusts.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Occasional strong to severe storms are possible into the evening. No watch is anticipated.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A line of storms has developed in northern Pennsylvania and is drifting south. While deep layer shear is weak (20 to 25 knots per CLE VWP), moderate instability (1000-1500 J/kg MLCAPE) and mid-level lapse rates around 7 C/km have proven sufficient for occasional stronger storms within this line. This should continue to be the case into the evening. However, the aforementioned weak shear should limit the longevity of any individual storms with more pulse type convection expected. Storms should struggle in eastern Pennsylvania as dewpoints have mixed into the low to mid 50s and MLCAPE is sufficiently less around 500 J/kg per RAP mesoanalysis. Therefore, the stronger storms are expected in western Pennsylvania and far eastern Ohio where instability is greater.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A new severe thunderstorm watch is likely needed soon in southeast Kansas and southwest Missouri.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Storms have formed on the western edge and slightly west of severe thunderstorm watch 307 where instability is maximized. Expect these storms to continue with additional development/upscale growth possible. Therefore, a new severe thunderstorm watch is likely needed to cover the threat in this region.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The threat for large hail and damaging winds continues in severe thunderstorm watch 305.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The cluster of storms in southeast Wisconsin has now mostly moved over the cool waters of Lake Michigan which should limit the severe threat while over the lake. In the wake of this convection, the boundary layer is stable in southeast Wisconsin should limit any additional severe weather threat. Farther south, rigorous updraft development has occurred across northern Illinois in an environment with MLCAPE around 1000 to 1500 J/kg and deep layer shear around 25 to 30 knots (per LOT VWP). This combination of instability and shear will continue to support multicell storm mode with a hail threat initially (Given the very steep mid-level lapse rates of 8.4 C/km per DVN 12Z RAOB). As storms eventually congeal, expect the damaging wind threat to increase. Storms have started to develop south of the current watch which may necessitate a local extension of WW305 across the LOT CWA. Trends will continue to be monitored to determine whether this will be necessary.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe weather threat is increasing across southwest Michigan as storms move in from Lake Michigan and additional storms develop.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A cluster off storms this afternoon in southeast Wisconsin have now moved over the cool waters of Lake Michigan and thus weakened. However, there are still thunderstorms and a remnant MCV associated with this cluster. The immediate Lake Michigan coastline remains stable, but temperatures have warmed into the mid 70s inland in the wake of earlier convection and MLCAPE has increased to over 1000 J/kg once again. This has led to new storm development near Kalamazoo and in northern Eaton county. While the eastern extent of this convection will likely be limited due to much more stable air in the wake of earlier convection, a small area of severe risk is possible in southwest Michigan from a combination of storms forming in that area now and expected rejuvenation of storms moving in from the west when they encounter the unstable airmass inland. Effective shear is around 30 to 35 knots per GRR VWP which should support mostly multicell storm mode. Mid-level lapse rates in excess of 8 C/km per 12Z DVN sounding will support large hail as the primary threat from isolated convection with wind damage expected to be the primary threat with the convection associated with the MCV. ..Bentley.. 06/01/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated large hail/severe gusts (55-65 mph) are possible this evening. The duration of the expected severe threat lends uncertainty whether a severe thunderstorm watch is warranted.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Radar mosaic shows a couple of intense storms on the west and north sides of the Metroplex. Surface temperatures are near 90 degrees F and dewpoints are near 70. Despite otherwise weak tropospheric flow in the lowest several km, large veering of the wind profile (reference KFWS VAD) beneath 25kt 500mb westerlies is yielding around 30-35kt effective shear. Around 2500 J/kg MLCAPE with a lower bound of a supercell wind profile will favor a mix of multicells and transient supercell structure. The more intense storms will be capable of isolated large hail (1.0-1.75 inches in diameter) and isolated severe gusts (55-65mph).

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe weather threat continues across severe thunderstorm watch 307 with a primary threat of large hail and damaging winds. The greatest severe weather coverage is expected in far eastern Missouri and far western Illinois and along the Kansas/Missouri border.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Several supercells have developed in northwest flow across portions of the Missouri Valley. Up to this point, storms have been confined to the greater instability (KS/MO border), and closer to the mid-level shortwave (NE MO and western IL). Storms have tried to form along the cold front between these two clusters but have struggled up to this point. Given we are past daytime heating and the strongest forcing is moving away from this area, storm coverage may remain quite sparse (as supported by the 21Z HRRR). Where strong updrafts have developed, storms have quickly taken on supercell structures, which is not surprising given around 70 knots of flow around 8km that is being sampled from the LSX and EAX VWP. Expect these supercells to continue through the evening with primarily a large hail threat, and eventual growth upscale and increasing damaging wind threat (including the St. Louis metro area). ..Bentley.. 06/01/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: It appears additional storm development and a longer-than-anticipated severe risk (into the evening hours) may yield a continued threat for large hail (1-2 inches in diameter)/severe gusts (60-70mph) for the next few hours. It is unclear whether a severe thunderstorm watch is warranted for the ongoing activity as it moves southeast this evening.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Radar imagery during the past 2 hours has shown a longer-lived severe storm near the Palmer Divide and it recently has shown a tendency to amass additional convection on the flanking line as it moves southeast. A left-mover near Pueblo recently developed and will likely pose a risk for large hail before interacting with the thunderstorm cluster to the north. Moist southeasterly upslope flow into the Palmer Divide cluster will probably enable storm persistence well into the evening. KPUB VAD showed 35kt westerly flow at 6km ARL which is resulting in around 45kt effective shear. Deep shear supportive of storm organization and a destabilized boundary layer over southeast CO suggest hail/wind may continue for the next few hours with the stronger storms.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Storms will likely develop and/or move into the TX South Plains this evening and pose a risk for large hail/severe gusts.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Surface analysis indicates a southwestward-moving outflow boundary over the southwestern part of the TX Panhandle extending southeastward into the TX Low Rolling Plains. Radar mosaic shows several left and right-moving supercells over southeastern NM with thunderstorms activity slowly encroaching on the TX South Plains this evening. KLBB VAD data shows 30kt westerly 500mb flow atop low-level southerlies yielding a wind profile supportive of storm organization. A warm/unstable boundary layer featuring temperatures well into the 80s and surface dewpoints ranging from the upper 50s northwest to the upper 60s southeast will likely prove favorable for storm development as existing activity moves towards the TX South Plains. Recent HRRR time-lagged guidance depicts a scenario for thunderstorms this evening as flow backs to southeasterly and strengthens this evening in response to a LLJ.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe storms will continue through the evening in northeast Indiana and northwest/north central Ohio. The primary threat will continue to be large hail, but occasional damaging wind gusts are possible.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A messy cluster of storms exists from northeast Indiana southeastward to north central Ohio on the western edge of the cold pool from earlier convection and on the eastern edge of the steeper (>8C/km) EML. Expect storms to continue in this area for the next few hours with a continued threat for mostly large hail. Eventually, these storms are expected to weaken as the low-level wind profile veers and the boundary layer stabilizes after dark. The 02Z watch expiration time appears okay for now, but an extension in time for an hour or two may be needed if any of these stronger storms persist beyond 02Z.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A cluster of storms is moving south toward St. Louis with an increasing damaging wind threat.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A cluster of supercells in Lincoln and Calhoun counties has started to congeal with an area of strong inbound velocities noted from KLSX in the RFD region of the easternmost supercell. This may be the beginning stages of a developing bowing segment as these storms continue to congeal. These storms are in an environment with MLCAPE around 1500 to 2000 J/kg and effective shear around 50 to 60 knots per LSX VWP which will continue to support storm organization into the overnight hours. MRMS MESH continues to show 1.5 to 2 inch hail with both of the supercells in this cluster. Therefore, the St. Louis metro area will be under a significant threat for both large hail and damaging winds for the next 1 to 2 hours, especially on the west side. ..Bentley.. 06/02/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Potential for strong surface gusts may continue, and could increase further, with an evolving convective system spreading into areas of northwest Texas, to the northwest and north of Abilene, through 3-4 AM. Trends are being monitored for the possibility of an additional severe weather watch to the southeast of severe thunderstorm watch 313.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Vigorous thunderstorm development persists along/above the leading edge of southeastward advancing conglomerate convective outflow. This includes a recent merging of the line with new cells forming just ahead of it, in response to forcing associated with low-level warm advection near a 30+ kt south-southeasterly 850 mb speed maximum, in the presence of moderate CAPE (on the order of 1000-2000 J/kg). Activity is embedded within fairly modest westerly deep-layer ambient mean flow on the order of 20-30 kt, but, due to veering of winds with height, shear within the convective layer appears strong. Although convection appears likely to gradually propagate east of the low-level jet axis over the course of the next few hours, vertical shear may remain sufficient to maintain organized convective development. This may become particularly focused along and just north of the outflow intersection with a preceding outflow boundary, which has stalled near/north of Snyder and Abilene, and may be accompanied by increasing potential for strong surface gusts through 08-09Z. ..Kerr.. 06/02/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe weather potential now appears to be in the process of diminishing. This seems likely to continue as convection spreads southeast of the Interstate 20 corridor to the west/southwest of the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex through daybreak. If current trends continue, the remaining valid portion of the watch could be cancelled within the next hour or two.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Strong to severe wind gusts near/north of Abilene into the Breckenridge vicinity appeared to accompany the evolution of a mesoscale convective vortex, and a strengthening rear inflow jet beneath the increasingly extensive trailing stratiform precipitation region of the evolving convective system. As the leading line progresses across and southeast of the Interstate 20 corridor to the southwest of the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex, a notable decrease in intensity is now readily evident in recent radar and lightning data. This seems likely to continue as activity encounters an environment more substantially impacted by prior convection, resulting in inflow of more stable air. Correspondingly, potential for strong surface gusts should also diminish. ..Kerr.. 06/02/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...
